record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: How do double-trace interfaces in boundary or defect conformal field theory fuse with one another?

evidence.quote: our aim for the near future is to investigate the fusion process of the presented double trace interfaces by these methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{CFT}_+$ and $\mathrm{CFT}_-$ be two large-$N$ conformal field theories in $d$ dimensions that are related by a relevant double-trace deformation: starting from a CFT containing a single-trace scalar primary $\mathcal{O}$ of scaling dimension $\Delta_-$, the deformation $\int d^d x\, \mathcal{O}^2$ triggers an RG flow whose IR endpoint is a CFT in which the corresponding operator has dimension $\Delta_+ = d - \Delta_-$. A double-trace interface is the planar codimension-one conformal interface $\mathcal{I}$ separating these two theories that is obtained by turning on the double-trace deformation only on a half-space; equivalently, it is described holographically by a bulk scalar in AdS$_{d+1}$ satisfying alternate boundary conditions on the two halves of the conformal boundary.

Given two such double-trace interfaces $\mathcal{I}_1$ and $\mathcal{I}_2$, placed on parallel planes at separation $\varepsilon \to 0$, describe the fusion product
$$\mathcal{I}_1 \star \mathcal{I}_2 := \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathcal{I}_1(x_d = \varepsilon)\, \mathcal{I}_2(x_d = 0),$$
including the renormalization of local interface operators and counterterms, the resulting conformal interface (or composite defect) between the appropriate pair of CFTs, the leading-$1/N$ fusion algebra they generate, the spectrum of operators on the fused interface, and the change in the interface contribution to the sphere partition function (the $g$-factor in $d=2$).
artifact.status_search_result: General frameworks for the fusion of conformal interfaces/defects exist (e.g. fusion of conformal interfaces in 2d, effective theory for fusion of conformal defects, and fusion of conformal defects in interacting theories). Recent work on RG interfaces from double-trace deformations (2024) addresses aspects of fusion in the holographic large-$N$ setting, but a complete computation of the fusion of two double-trace interfaces (with full renormalized operator spectrum and $g$-factor change) does not appear to have been carried out in full generality, so the question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: RG Interfaces from Double-Trace Deformations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses RG interfaces obtained from double-trace deformations and their properties including fusion-related aspects.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats double-trace RG interfaces, addressing fusion-type questions partially.

status_evidence.title: Fusion of conformal defects in interacting theories
status_evidence.snippet: General results on the fusion of conformal defects in interacting CFTs, including renormalization in the fusion limit.
status_evidence.claim: General fusion framework for conformal defects exists but is not specialized fully to double-trace interfaces.

status_evidence.title: Double trace interfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs double-trace interfaces and computes their leading large-N data, posing fusion as a future direction.
status_evidence.claim: The construction is known, but fusion of two such interfaces was originally posed as an open direction.
